focus: Illustrate first-order radioactive decay with N(t)=N0 exp(-lambda t). Let learners set initial amount, nonnegative decay constant, and time; show remaining fraction and amount, and compare the half-life time ln(2)/lambda. State that the deterministic curve describes expected bulk behavior, not an individual random decay event.
audience: A second-year engineering undergraduate familiar with exponentials, logarithms, and simple rates of change.
excerpt: Paraphrase, not a quotation: the practice case uses the standard first-order decay model dN/dt = -lambda N and its exponential solution. This equation is the teaching calculation; the linked 1903 paper is the historical source context, not a verified transcription of this modern notation.
section: Rutherford and Soddy (1903), Radioactive Change, Philosophical Magazine 5(29), pp. 576–591. Publisher record is identifiable, but its full text returned an access error in this audit; this locator is therefore bibliographic, not text-verified.
